links.outcome: Reading level of chatbot responses to patient vascular surgery questions
links.effect: ChatGPT Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 14.5 ± 2.2, Gunning Fog 17.7 ± 3.1 (post-secondary education); Bard 8.2 ± 1.7 and 11.0 ± 2.0 (high-school).
links.quote: The mean Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, and Gunning Fog Index of ChatGPT responses were 29.4 ± 10.8, 14.5 ± 2.2, and 17.7 ± 3.1, respectively, indicating that responses were readable with a post-secondary education.

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses versus plain-language comprehension
links.effect: ChatGPT responses readable only at post-secondary level (FRE 29.4, FKGL 14.5); Bard at high-school level (FRE 58.9, FKGL 8.2).
links.quote: Bard's mean readability scores were 58.9 ± 10.5, 8.2 ± 1.7, and 11.0 ± 2.0, respectively, indicating that responses were readable with a high-school education (p < .0001 for three metrics).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates LLM chatbots (ChatGPT-3.5 and Google Bard) answering mock vascular surgery patient questions, with clinician expert grading of accuracy, completeness, appropriateness, and readability, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
